info.title: DivvyHQ
info.description:
This is the developer documentation page for DivvyHQ's Enterprise Accounts API.
DivvyHQ is a content planning and production workflow platform for marketing and content teams. For DivvyHQ clients and other interested parties, our RESTful API can be used to request data, perform specific actions or build connections with other content or marketing-centric applications. Programming skills are required.
If you’re ready to roll, our documentation should provide a good roadmap.
General information can be found [here](https://help.divvyhq.com/hc/en-us/categories/204517927-Knowledge-Base-FAQs).
## How to use
We recommend you use the API Key token authentication method when interacting with the API. For this you will have to send an `Authorization` header (It must be UTF-8 encoded) along with each request in the following format:
`Authorization` `apikey [username email]:[api key generated from My Profile section of the app]`.
For example:
Header name: `Authorization`
Header value: `apikey bob@example.com:671077f87c7d1716d666ea8f96ab5bf4b5776389`
Alternatively, you can send the username and API key as query parameters in the form of `?username=bob@example.com&api_key=671077f87c7d1716d666ea8f96ab5bf4b5776389`.
Need your keys? [Watch this video to get you started](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n1136fC58ag).
Unless specified otherwise the page size of the endpoints is 200 results per page.
## Overview
The main resources are: Myself, Team Members, Simple Calendars, Content Items and Campaigns.

### Myself
This is a special endpoint. It returns rich information about the currently authenticated Team Member, whom the API key used to access the API belongs to. It is basically an hydrated Team Member resource with information about the account and some settings. This is a singleton resource, meaning it will always return a collection with a single result.

### Team Members
This endpoint returns all the Team Members of the authenticated Team Member's account that are visible to her depending on roles assigned and whether or not she is an administrator.

### Simple Calendars
Simple Calendars are used to organize content and contain information about the Content Strategies allowed in the Content Items that belong to them.

### Content Items
Content Items always belong to Simple Calendars.

### Calendar Entries
This is a read only endpoint that provides the necessary information to populate a calendar.

## About types
If you need to know which data types are returned and required by each endpoint you can send an OPTIONS request to that endpoint (You still need to provide credentials).

get.description:
Read only endpoint which exposes all the necessary information
needed to populate a calendar.
This flattens Content Items, Campaigns, Production Tasks, Reminders and
Social Posts into a single queryable endpoint. The `kind` attribute
is used to differentiate between them.

post.description:
This endpoint is used to request a filtered list of Calendar Entries.
It is NOT used to create Calendar Entries.

This endpoint allows filtering of Calendar Entries by performing a
POST request with the filter parameters included in the POST body
instead of a GET request with filters as query parameters.
The reason behind this design is that filter parameters could be
longer than the character limit the URL admits.
Note that the Calendar Entries cannot be queried in a particular order.

`kind` field possible values:

- `KIND_CONTENT_ITEM_PROMOTION = 1`
- `KIND_CONTENT_ITEM_MAINTENANCE = 2`
- `KIND_CONTENT_ITEM_DEADLINE = 3`
- `KIND_PRODUCTION_TASK_START_BY = 4`
- `KIND_PRODUCTION_TASK_DEADLINE = 5`
- `KIND_CAMPAIGN = 6`
- `KIND_REMINDER = 7`
- `KIND_SOCIAL_POST_DATE = 8`
